intro: Pergamon was a royal capital set high on a steep acropolis. This ancient city in İzmir province takes us back to the 3rd century BC, and it is home to the steepest theatre of the ancient world. Ready to climb into its story?
history: Pergamon was the capital of the Attalid dynasty, and its library of 200,000 scrolls gave a whole writing material its name: parchment. Then, in 133 BC, the city was bequeathed to Rome. Under its new masters it became famous for a very different kind of place: the Asklepion, its healing centre.
structure-2: You are now on the Great Altar terrace. It was less an altar than a stage: the 113-metre Gigantomachy frieze wrapped the building in a battle told in stone. Between 1878 and 1886 it was dismantled and shipped to Berlin. What stands at Pergamon now is the terrace and the footings. Pause for a moment and picture that stone battle once circling this very spot.
structure-5: Here stands the Red Basilica, the great brick complex of Pergamon. Step back and take in its scale, and imagine it in another age, when this was a sanctuary of the Egyptian gods.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Acropolis and the Temple of Trajan, and save time for the Asklepion, where healing was the city's art.
facts: Did you know? The word 'parchment' comes from Pergamon: when Egypt cut off the papyrus, the city perfected treated skins instead. The acropolis theatre is the steepest of the ancient world, with 80 rows pitched almost like a cliff and seating for 10,000. At the Asklepion, treatment meant dream interpretation, water cures and theatre, and Galen, the physician, trained here. As for the Great Altar, it was dismantled and shipped to Berlin between 1878 and 1886; it is the building the Pergamon Museum is named after.
outro: This brings our journey through Pergamon to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
